facts.statement: The IFSCA (TechFin and Ancillary Services) Regulations, 2025 (notification IFSCA/GN/2025/005) were notified on 8 July 2025 as a unified framework for TechFins and Ancillary Services supporting financial services under Section 3(1)(e)(i)-(xi) of the IFSCA Act.

TAS Regulations chapters: II Registration, III Fit and Proper Requirements and Code of Conduct, IV Requirement of Principal Officer and Compliance Officer, V Intermediaries and Service Recipients, VI Miscellaneous, with Schedules I, III and IV.
facts.detail: The Third Schedule lists prohibited/excluded services.

facts.statement: Under TAS 2025 a Group Entity requires 20% or more equity/capital contribution; a Network is a pooled-resource firm structure; an intermediary passes TAS services to service recipients without additional layers and the flow must be demonstrable and traceable.

TAS fit-and-proper criteria are enhanced versus BATF: they include chargesheet by an Indian or foreign enforcement agency, charges framed by a court, debarment orders currently in force (not merely a 3-year lookback), and material-impact determination reserved to the Authority.
facts.detail: Registration remains valid until suspended, cancelled, or voluntarily surrendered with Authority approval.

facts.statement: Eligible TAS legal forms: company, LLP incorporated in IFSC, branch of an Indian or foreign company/LLP, and a partnership firm registered under the Indian Partnership Act 1932 where all partners are members of professional bodies.

TAS in-principle approval conditions must be fulfilled within 180 days (extendable); existing entities must migrate within 12 months of TAS commencement, extendable to a maximum of 24 months by the Chairperson; failure to obtain Certificate of Registration within 12 months makes the approval/authorisation deemed invalid and operations must cease.

TAS Principal Officer and Compliance Officer must be full-time and IFSC-based; the PO is optional for entities serving exclusively Group Entities in IFSC subject to Authority approval; professional-body members who are not employees may serve as PO/CO but cannot simultaneously serve another IFSC unit.

After the 24-month transition, TAS repeals the Ancillary Services Framework (10 February 2021) and the TechFin authorisation clause of the FinTech Entity Framework (27 April 2022); reporting currency is USD with operations in specified foreign currency.
facts.detail: BATF software development is covered under TAS when service recipients are BATF providers in IFSC or outside India.

facts.statement: The TAS draft was released 9 May 2025 with comments due 1 June 2025; its objective is to make GIFT-IFSC a Regional Financial Capability Hub in the short term and a Global Financial Capability Hub long term.

The BATF (Book-keeping, Accounting, Taxation and Financial Crime Compliance Services) Regulations, 2024 (notification IFSCA/GN/2024/003, 4 June 2024) permit only company or LLP legal forms with promoters from non-FATF-blacklisted jurisdictions.

BATF Principal Officer qualifications: CA/CS/CMA/CPA/CFA or equivalent PG degree in finance, accountancy, commerce, economics, taxation or law, with minimum 5 years experience; Compliance Officer minimum 3 years; the FCC Principal Officer needs an additional FCC qualification.

BATF safeguards: minimum 60 sq ft carpet office area per employee; operations and balance sheet in specified foreign currency with an INR account allowed for admin/statutory expenses; independent CA/CS/CMA compliance certificate within 90 days of FY closure; employees transferred from Indian group entities capped at 20% of total workforce for 10 consecutive FYs; no transfer of assets from Indian group entities.

Ancillary Service Providers had 3 years to obtain BATF registration and 6 months to comply with PO/CO and office-space requirements; relaxation processing under BATF takes 60 days from a complete application.

IFSCA has three sandbox types: the FinTech Regulatory Sandbox (FRS, live environment with regulatory exemptions), the FinTech Innovation Sandbox (FIS, isolated/non-live early-stage development), and the Inter-Operable Regulatory Sandbox (IoRS, cross-sector).

Sandbox application is two-stage (Preliminary assessed in 30 working days, then Final); in-principle conditions must be fulfilled within 90 days with at least one Testing Partner; testing lasts a maximum of 12 months extendable by 6; records are retained 7 years from exit; the final report is due within 30 days of testing-stage expiry; there are 11 revocation grounds.

Sandbox eligibility (India): company/LLP/branch, DPIIT-registered startup, domestic-regulator-regulated entity, or academic-institution affiliate; foreign applicants must not be from FATF-blacklisted jurisdictions. Annexure I permissible activities: capital markets, banking, insurance, pension, metals and commodities, foreign university, financial support services and compliance/supervision thereof.
facts.detail: Fit-and-proper look-back is 8 years for functionaries; shareholders with 10%+ holding require KYC disclosure.

facts.statement: Industry feedback benchmarked the IFSCA sandbox against UK FCA, Singapore MAS Sandbox Plus (grant up to S$500,000), HKMA and Australia ASIC ERS (up to 24 months), recommending mandatory compensation arrangements, PI insurance, independent dispute resolution and a published relaxation guidance note.

The IFSCA Informal Guidance Scheme, 2024 (circular IFSCA-LPRA/11/2024) is effective 1 January 2025 with two instruments - No-Action Letter and Interpretive Letter - fee USD 1,000, disposal endeavoured within 30 days (excluding applicant response time), and applicant queries to be answered within 15 days.
facts.detail: Guidance is non-binding, not appealable, and not a conclusive determination; confidentiality is available for 90 days on specific request with possible name redaction.

facts.statement: Informal guidance may be rejected for hypothetical queries, questions of general nature, no direct interest of the applicant, sub-judice matters, enforcement already initiated, or similar guidance already issued; fraud or misrepresentation renders the guidance non-est.

The IFSC Cybersecurity and Cyber Resilience consultation (September 2024) is principle-based with proportionality, has five pillars (Governance, Cyber Framework, Third-Party Risk, Communication/Awareness, Audit), mandates a CISO/Designated Officer and Governing Board cyber expertise, and requires audits by CERT-In empanelled auditors.
facts.detail: The Cyber Security Advisory Committee is chaired by Dr. Sanjay Bahl, DG CERT-In (constituted August 2023).

facts.statement: The IFSCA Global In-House Centres Regulations, 2025 were notified 24 December 2025 replacing the GIC Regulations 2020; GICs were recognised as a 'Financial Service' by MoF notification dated 16 October 2020.

GIHC rules: legal forms company/LLP/branch; operating models Captive, BOT, JV, Hybrid or IFSCA-permitted; group-entity relationship at 20%+ equity/capital; Indian group entities capped at 10% of the GIC Unit's total revenue per FY; service recipients must be non-residents and not from FATF-blacklisted jurisdictions; PO and CO full-time IFSC-based. GIHCs are distinct from GRCTCs (Finance Company Regs 2021) and from GCCs.
facts.detail: The December 2025 regulations removed the earlier employee-transfer cap.
